evals.name: Secret management choice for a GitOps repo

expectations.text: Rejects plain Secrets in Git, and states that base64 is encoding not encryption — anyone with repo read access has the credential
expectations.evidence: **`base64` is an encoding, not encryption.** `echo cGFzc3dvcmQxMjM= | base64 -d` is the entire attack.

expectations.text: Presents the real options with trade-offs: Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, SOPS, and Vault (via CSI or ESO)
expectations.evidence: | **External Secrets Operator** | ... | **Secrets Store CSI driver + Vault provider** | ... | **Sealed Secrets** |

expectations.text: Notes that External Secrets Operator / Vault keep the secret out of Git entirely, whereas Sealed Secrets and SOPS commit an encrypted form
expectations.evidence: Three options, all of which keep the *reference* in Git and the *value* out of it.

expectations.text: Mentions that Argo CD needs to be able to decrypt or resolve whichever mechanism is chosen
expectations.evidence: The generated `Secret` does not exist until the ESO controller reconciles the `ExternalSecret`. A pod starting in the same sync wave will `CreateContainerConfigError`.

expectations.text: Does not simply say 'use Sealed Secrets' without stating why it fits or does not fit their situation
expectations.evidence: **Sealed Secrets** is much less to run, but the controller's private key is now a single point of failure you must back up

expectations.text: Compares the real options rather than asserting one — app-of-apps, ApplicationSet, monorepo, multi-repo, environment-branch — with trade-offs
expectations.evidence: 18 Applications is borderline — app-of-apps would survive it — but you'll add service 7 and env 4, and auto-discovery is what makes that a directory creation instead of a PR full of near-identical YAML.

expectations.text: Recommends ApplicationSet for the 6 services x 3 envs x 2 clusters fan-out instead of hand-maintained Application manifests, and explains that generators remove the per-combination manifest
expectations.evidence: one **ApplicationSet with a git directory generator** per repo

expectations.text: Separates platform/cluster addons from application workloads (different ownership, different review path, often a different AppProject)
expectations.evidence: **`platform-config`** — cluster addons. Owned by the platform team, with its own Git access control and its own AppProject.

expectations.text: Addresses environment promotion explicitly — directory-per-env vs branch-per-env — and notes the trade-off rather than silently picking one
expectations.evidence: **Do not use environment branches.** They're the obvious next step from where you are and they're the trap: branch drift between staging and prod is invisible until it bites

expectations.text: Warns against targetRevision: HEAD for production regardless of pattern chosen
expectations.evidence: absent

expectations.text: Flags at least one anti-pattern relevant to their current layout (e.g. a flat directory of hand-edited Applications does not scale, or mixing platform and tenant resources in one AppProject)
expectations.evidence: **one repo is carrying two different ownership boundaries**... Wildcards in `sourceRepos` or `destinations` are the single most common way an AppProject ends up decorative.

expectations.text: Expresses the window as a cron schedule plus a duration, not a start/end time pair
expectations.evidence:
schedule: '0 8 * * 1-5'
      duration: 10h

expectations.text: States the combination rule correctly: with both allow and deny windows present, a sync must fall INSIDE an allow window AND OUTSIDE every deny window
expectations.evidence: **Any active `deny` window wins.** Automated sync is blocked. ... Otherwise, **an active `allow` window** permits sync ... if allow windows exist but **none is currently active**, automated sync is blocked

expectations.text: Sets manualSync: true on the deny window so on-call can still sync by hand during the freeze
expectations.evidence: kind: deny ... manualSync: true          # REQUIRED for on-call to sync during the freeze

expectations.text: Explains manualSync correctly as an escape hatch that PERMITS manual syncs the window would otherwise block — not as an additional restriction, and not as something that enables automated sync
expectations.evidence: `manualSync` is an escape hatch, not an extra restriction — the CRD defines it as *"enables manual syncs when they would otherwise be blocked."*

expectations.text: Does not claim manualSync: false adds protection beyond the window's default behaviour (false is the default and blocks manual syncs too)
expectations.evidence: Setting `manualSync: false` there (as a naive reading suggests, and as the "stricter" instinct suggests) gives you a freeze that locks out the people meant to break it

evals.name: AppProject resource allow/deny lists and sourceNamespaces scoping

expectations.text: sourceRepos lists the specific repo URL, not '*'
expectations.evidence:
sourceRepos:
    - https://github.com/acme/payments.git

expectations.text: destinations scope both namespaces to the in-cluster server (https://kubernetes.default.svc), not server: '*'
expectations.evidence:
destinations:
    - server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
      namespace: payments-dev
    - server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
      namespace: payments-prod

expectations.text: Uses clusterResourceWhitelist for the cluster-scoped allowance, listing Namespace (group "") — and does NOT use a namespace-scoped list for this
expectations.evidence:
clusterResourceWhitelist:
    - group: ''
      kind: Namespace

expectations.text: Uses namespaceResourceBlacklist for ResourceQuota and LimitRange — correctly distinguishing namespace-scoped denial from the cluster-scoped whitelist
expectations.evidence: Both are core-group (group: '') and namespaced — they belong here, not in clusterResourceBlacklist.

expectations.text: Sets spec.sourceNamespaces to include payments-dev so Application CRs outside the Argo CD namespace are permitted by this project
expectations.evidence:
sourceNamespaces:
    - payments-dev

expectations.text: Notes that sourceNamespaces on the AppProject is not sufficient on its own — the Argo CD instance must also be configured to watch that namespace (application-namespaces / .spec.sourceNamespaces on the ArgoCD CR)
expectations.evidence: On OpenShift GitOps that is `ArgoCD.spec.sourceNamespaces` on the operator CR (`argoproj.io/v1beta1`)

expectations.text: Does not use a wildcard in clusterResourceWhitelist (no '*'/'*'), which would defeat the restriction
expectations.evidence:
Cluster-scoped: Namespace and nothing else.
  # A non-empty whitelist is already deny-by-default for everything absent.

evals.name: AppProject role scoping and orphaned resource monitoring

expectations.text: Defines spec.roles with a named role and policy lines, not cluster-level RBAC
expectations.evidence:
roles:
    - name: developer
      description: Payments team — read and sync, no delete

expectations.text: Policy lines use the p, proj:<project>:<role>, applications, <action>, <project>/<app>, allow form — scoped to this project, not '*'
expectations.evidence: p, proj:payments:developer, applications, get, payments/*, allow

expectations.text: Grants get and sync actions and does NOT grant delete
expectations.evidence:
- p, proj:payments:developer, applications, sync, payments/*, allow
        # Explicit denials
        - p, proj:payments:developer, applications, delete, payments/*, deny

expectations.text: Binds the role to a group via the role's groups list (OIDC/SSO group), rather than assuming a Kubernetes RoleBinding grants Argo CD UI access
expectations.evidence:
groups:
        - payments-team            # must match the group claim your SSO emits

expectations.text: Enables spec.orphanedResources with warn: true
expectations.evidence:
orphanedResources:
    warn: true

expectations.text: Uses the orphanedResources ignore list to exclude ServiceAccount and ConfigMap kinds, rather than disabling orphaned-resource monitoring entirely
expectations.evidence: Name-scoped entries are deliberate. Ignoring `kind: ServiceAccount` and `kind: ConfigMap` wholesale would silence exactly the orphans you want to see

expectations.text: Does not conflate Argo CD project RBAC with Kubernetes RBAC — states that project roles govern access within Argo CD, not cluster permissions
expectations.evidence: An AppProject role is additive to `argocd-rbac-cm` and only binds to **OIDC/SSO groups** (`groups:`) or project JWT tokens — not to local Argo CD users.
